entries.topic: How the Christian canon was listed, c.180-1546: Irenaeus, Muratorian, Origen, Eusebius, Athanasius, Carthage, Jerome, Trent

claims.text: Irenaeus (c.180) argued the gospels cannot be 'either more or fewer' than four, citing four zones of the world, four principal winds and the four-faced cherubim; he rejected the Valentinians' 'comparatively recent' Gospel of Truth as 'totally unlike' the apostolic gospels
Muratorian fragment: single poor Latin copy found by Muratori; usually dated 170-200, some redate to the 4th c.

Muratorian fragment accepts Wisdom of Solomon and the apocalypses of John and Peter ('some of us are not willing that the latter be read in church'); Shepherd written 'very recently, in our times', ought to be read but not publicly in church; rejects letters to Laodiceans and Alexandrians 'forged in Paul's name' for Marcion's heresy ('gall... mixed with honey'); accepts nothing of Arsinous, Valentinus, Miltiades, Basilides

Origen (via Eusebius HE VI.25): four gospels 'the only indisputable ones in the Church of God under heaven'; OT canonical books 'as the Hebrews have handed them down, are twenty-two'; 2 Peter doubtful; 2-3 John not all consider genuine; Hebrews: 'God knows' who wrote it
Serapion of Antioch first let the Rhossus congregation read the Gospel of Peter, then on reading it found additions he judged unorthodox and wrote against it (Eusebius HE VI.12)

Eusebius HE III.25: recognized (4 gospels, Acts, Paul's epistles, 1 John, 1 Peter, Revelation 'if it seem proper'); disputed (James, Jude, 2 Peter, 2-3 John); spurious (Acts of Paul, Shepherd, Apocalypse of Peter, Barnabas, Teachings of the Apostles, Gospel of the Hebrews); heretical (Gospels of Peter, Thomas, Matthias; Acts of Andrew, John) 'absurd and impious'

Athanasius 367: 22 OT books incl. Baruch and 'the epistle', Esther not in the 22; 27 NT books; 'fountains of salvation'; second group to be read (Wisdom, Sirach, Esther, Judith, Tobit, Teaching of the Apostles, Shepherd); apocrypha 'an invention of heretics'

Carthage 419 canon 24 'That nothing be read in church besides the Canonical Scripture' lists Tobit, Judith, two books of Maccabees, five books of Solomon, 14 epistles of Paul, Revelation; to be sent to Boniface (bishop of Rome) for confirmation; canon 46 allows passions of martyrs on anniversaries

Jerome's Prologus Galeatus (391-392) set Wisdom, Sirach, Judith, Tobias and the Shepherd 'among the apocrypha'; preface to Solomon books: the Church reads Judith, Tobit, Maccabees but does not admit them among canonical Scriptures, reads Wisdom and Sirach 'for the edification of the people, not to give authority to doctrines'
Gallagher 2015: in the Judith preface Jerome says the Nicene synod is read to have counted Judith among the Holy Scriptures ('sinodus nicena in numero Sanctarum Scripturarum legitur conputasse')

'Deuterocanonical' coined 1566 by Sixtus of Siena; Cajetan and Seripando among Catholic figures who followed Jerome in rejecting the books; 3 and 4 Esdras and Prayer of Manasses printed in an apocrypha section of the Sixto-Clementine Vulgate; Anglican Articles: read 'for example of life' not doctrine
Eusebius HE III.3: 'Paul's fourteen epistles are well known and undisputed'; some reject Hebrews 'saying that it is disputed by the church of Rome'

entries.topic: Books left out: who excluded each and in what document; counts

claims.text: Irenaeus: the Marcosians 'adduce an unspeakable number of apocryphal and spurious writings, which they themselves have forged'
Irenaeus: the Cainites 'produce a fictitious history of this kind, which they style the Gospel of Judas'
Origen, Homily 1 on Luke: the Church has four gospels only, heresy several; names Gospel of the Egyptians, of the Twelve, of Basilides, of Thomas, of Matthias

Decretum Gelasianum ch.5 lists 62 entries 'not received', incl. Gospels of Matthias, Barnabas, James the younger, Peter, 'Thomas which the Manichaeans use', Bartholomew, Andrew; Acts of Andrew, Thomas, Peter, Philip; the Shepherd; Revelations of Paul, Thomas, Stephen; Assumption of Mary; Testament of Job; daughters of Adam 'Leptogeneseos'; also works of Tertullian, Clement of Alexandria, Eusebius's History, Lactantius, Cassian; its OT list includes Tobit, Judith, two Maccabees, Wisdom, Ecclesiasticus. Tally (this book): 11 gospel entries, 7 acts, 3 revelations = 21 of 62

Dobschütz: Decretum is 'no genuine decree... of Damasus or Gelasius, but a pseudonymous literary production' of 519-553; manuscripts attribute it to Damasus, Gelasius or Hormisdas; compiler probably southern Gallic; circulated in e.g. 8th-c. Ragyndrudis Codex
Codex Sinaiticus (mid-4th c., not before c.325) includes Epistle of Barnabas and part of the Shepherd of Hermas after the NT; OT includes Tobit, Judith, 1 and 4 Maccabees, Wisdom, Sirach
Jubilees known also as 'Little Genesis'; canonical for Ethiopian and Eritrean Tewahedo churches and Beta Israel; about fifteen scrolls at Qumran
Constantine's letter (Socrates I.9): 'if any treatise composed by Arius should be discovered, let it be consigned to the flames'; concealment penalty 'death'
Codex Tchacos found in the 1970s near Maghagha; National Geographic unveiled the first English translation of the Gospel of Judas on 6 April 2006

entries.topic: Protestant, Catholic, Eastern Orthodox and Ethiopian canons compared

claims.text: Luther's 1522 September Testament placed Hebrews, James, Jude and Revelation after the other NT books as disputed; called James an 'epistle of straw'; 1534 Bible grouped OT deuterocanon as Apocrypha 'not considered equal to the Holy Scriptures'; Lutheran Confessions define no canon

Orthodox use the Septuagint; Synod of Jerusalem 1672 canons widely accepted; Greek, Russian, Georgian Bibles add 1 Esdras, 3 Maccabees, Psalm 151; Prayer of Manasseh (end of 2 Chronicles in Russian/Georgian); 4 Maccabees appendix; Russian adds 3 Ezdras; Trullan synod 692 endorsed lists that 'do not agree'; Peshitta NT 22 books
OrthodoxWiki: Orthodox OT canon not formally defined by an ecumenical council; Jerusalem 1672 regional, not pan-Orthodox; numbered list of 49 OT books plus 4 Maccabees appendix
Eastern and Oriental Orthodox OT up to 49 books; Catholic 46; Protestant 39
